- uses: DeterminateSystems/determinate-nix-action@v3.21.9
          with:
              # Add the cache and its trusted key at install time, so the daemon starts already knowing
              # them. Adding them afterwards in the Configure step proved ineffective — the daemon never
              # queried cachet at all — because a substituter and its trusted key reach the daemon only when
              # it reads its config at start. extra-substituters and extra-trusted-public-keys accumulate
              # (they use the extra- prefix), so this adds cachet alongside cache.nixos.org rather than
              # replacing it.
              extra-conf: |
                  extra-substituters = ${{ inputs.cache-url }}
                  extra-trusted-public-keys = ${{ inputs.trusted-public-key }}

        # Log out of FlakeHub, which the determinate-nix-action step above logged into on its own. On a
        # runner granting id-token: write — which this action requires to mint its own cachet OIDC token —
        # Determinate mints a second OIDC token for FlakeHub and logs in, and that login adds
        # https://cache.flakehub.com to the daemon's active substituters. This deployment is not a FlakeHub
        # Cache customer, so every narinfo lookup then answers 401 ("User is not authorized for this
        # resource") before it falls through to cachet: an error-level log line and a wasted round trip on
        # every request, on a build that still succeeds. Logging out returns the substituter set to the
        # logged-out state, in which cache.flakehub.com is absent — verified against a local Determinate
        # install, where `determinate-nixd status` reports logged-out and `nix config show substituters`
        # omits FlakeHub. cachet's own read credential is the netrc merged from additionalNetrcSources and
        # is independent of the FlakeHub login, so the Configure step's auth probe below still reports 404.
        - name: Log out of FlakeHub Cache, which this deployment does not use
          shell: bash
          run: |
              set -euo pipefail
              # `|| true`: a job without id-token never logged in, so logout is a no-op there rather than a
              # failure, and this action must not fail a build over a cache it does not even use.
              sudo determinate-nixd auth logout || true
              echo "cachet: FlakeHub login status after logout:"
              sudo determinate-nixd status || true

        - name: Configure cachet

content.text:
It doesn't solve it — `cachet-action` has the identical setup and would show the identical warning. Same `determinate-nix-action@v3.21.9`, same provision-then-logout dance.

But its comments are much more explicit than the in-repo copy, and they answer the thing I said I was unsure about:

> Determinate synthesizes the netrc the daemon reads at daemon start, merging every file under `additionalNetrcSources` — and that start-up synthesis is the only reliable one on these runners. **A later re-synthesis is gated on the FlakeHub login, whose transient failures otherwise leave cache reads at 401 and every build recompiling from source.**

So the write-config-before-install ordering isn't incidental — it's a deliberate defense against this exact FlakeHub failure. The warning you're seeing is the failure that design already survives. That's why builds stay green.

Which reframes the choice. It's not "warning vs. Determinate's benefits" — it's that **the entire netrc dance exists because of Determinate**, and dropping it removes the hazard rather than just muting the symptom:

| | Determinate (today) | `determinate: false` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FlakeHub login | attempted, fails, warns | never attempted |
| Credential delivery | `additionalNetrcSources` + start-up synthesis, ordered before install | `netrc-file = /etc/nix/netrc` in `extra-conf` |
| Logout step | required | gone |
| Re-synthesis gated on FlakeHub | real hazard, worked around by ordering | doesn't exist |

Three things I'd still flag before you pick:

1. `nix-installer-action` with `determinate: false` still uses Determinate's *installer* — you keep the fast, reliable install, you just don't get Determinate Nix the product (its daemon management, its GC).
2. I haven't verified `netrc-file` via `extra-conf` on a real runner. It's standard nix and the old TS implementation used exactly that shape in `nix.custom.conf`, but I'd want a CI run proving the auth probe still reports 404 before calling it done.
3. Whatever you pick should land in both this repo's `action/` and `cachet-action`, or they'll drift.

Want me to prototype option 1 on a branch so we get a real CI signal on the probe, or would you rather keep Determinate and I file the unconditional-login behaviour upstream?

          echo "extra-substituters = ${CACHET_CACHE_URL%/}"

Build only what dist ships, and stop asking FlakeHub for a login

Two CI defects, neither of them new.

dist builds `cargo build --workspace`, which includes cachet-worker: a
wasm32-only crate that fails a host build by construction, because its
manifest supplies getrandom under cfg(target_arch = "wasm32") and the
code names it unconditionally. That the release pipeline ever worked was
luck. Cargo keeps compiling in-flight units after a failure, so the run
succeeded whenever cachet-cli finished linking before cachet-worker
aborted, and failed when it did not. v0.0.6 hit the identical error and
passed; v0.0.7 failed once, then passed on a re-run with nothing changed.
`precise-builds = true` makes dist build `--package=cachet-cli`, which is
the only package it ships.

The installer logs in to FlakeHub on every job granting id-token: write,
which this action requires for its own OIDC token. This deployment is not
a FlakeHub customer, so the login cannot succeed: it warned on every job,
for every consumer, and the substituter it would have added answers 401
before every lookup falls through to cachet. There is no input that keeps
Determinate Nix and skips the login: determinate-nix-action is one step,
nix-installer-action with `determinate: true` hardcoded, and that input's
own description is "install Determinate Nix AND log in to FlakeHub".

So the action installs plain nix instead, which also deletes the
workaround the old shape needed. Determinate synthesizes the daemon's
netrc at start-up from `additionalNetrcSources`, and a later re-synthesis
is gated on the FlakeHub login, so a failed login could strand cache
reads at 401; the credential was written before the installer ran
specifically to dodge that. Plain nix reads `netrc-file` from its own
config, so the credential rides `extra-conf` with the substituter and the
trusted key, and the logout step and the config.json merge both go away.

`cachet setup` is untouched and stays Determinate-aware: it already
branches on whether the host runs Determinate Nix, registering the netrc
through `additionalNetrcSources` there and writing `netrc-file`
otherwise. A laptop installed the easy way keeps working.

gh pr create --title "Build only what dist ships, and stop asking FlakeHub for a login" --body "$(cat <<'MD'
Two CI defects, neither introduced by #18 — both were latent and #18 only changed the odds on one of them.

## The release pipeline was a coin flip

dist builds `cargo build --workspace`. That includes `cachet-worker`, which **cannot build for a host by construction**: its manifest supplies `getrandom` only under `cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")`, and CLAUDE.md §4 states the crate fails host builds and is excluded from `default-members`.

So every release run has been compiling a crate that errors. It passed anyway because cargo keeps compiling in-flight units after a failure — if `cachet-cli` finished linking first, dist found the binary and the job went green.

The evidence:

- **v0.0.6** (`32805833017`, x86_64-linux, *success*): same `error[E0433]: cannot find module or crate getrandom`, same two lines in `gc.rs` and `oauth.rs`.
- **v0.0.7** first attempt: same error, but `× failed to find bin cachet` — the abort won the race. Adding zstd to `cachet-push` made `cachet-cli` slower to compile, which is why it lost this time.
- **v0.0.7 re-run**: passed with nothing changed.

`precise-builds = true` makes dist build `--package=cachet-cli`. Verified locally:

```
building aarch64-apple-darwin target, using cargo profile dist --package=cachet-cli)
```

`cachet-worker` is never compiled.

## FlakeHub logs in on every job and cannot succeed

Every job in every consumer's CI prints:

```
Error: failed to update netrc via determinate-nixd: Login failure: Transient authentication mechanism error
##[warning]FlakeHub Login failure: The process '/usr/local/bin/determinate-nixd' failed with exit code 1
```

It isn't transient. On a runner granting `id-token: write` — which this action requires for its own OIDC token — Determinate mints a second token and logs in to FlakeHub. This deployment isn't a FlakeHub customer, so it can't succeed, and the substituter it would have added answers 401 before every lookup falls through to cachet.

There is no way to keep Determinate Nix and skip it. `determinate-nix-action` is a single composite step wrapping `nix-installer-action` with `determinate: true` hardcoded, and that input's own description is *"Whether to install Determinate Nix **and** log in to FlakeHub"*. One flag, both behaviours.

So the action installs plain nix (`determinate: false`), which also removes a workaround the old shape needed. Determinate synthesizes the daemon's netrc at start-up from `additionalNetrcSources`, and a **later re-synthesis is gated on the FlakeHub login** — a failed login could strand cache reads at 401 and send every build back to compiling from source. Writing the credential before the installer ran was specifically dodging that. Plain nix reads `netrc-file` from its own config, so:

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FlakeHub login | attempted, fails, warns | never attempted |
| Credential | `/etc/determinate/config.json` + `additionalNetrcSources` | `netrc-file = /etc/nix/netrc` in `extra-conf` |
| Logout step | required | gone |
| Re-synthesis gated on FlakeHub | real hazard, dodged by ordering | doesn't exist |

## `cachet setup` is untouched

The laptop path is independent of this and stays Determinate-aware — `crates/cachet-cli/src/setup.rs` already branches on whether the host runs Determinate Nix, registering the netrc through `additionalNetrcSources` there and writing `netrc-file` otherwise. Someone who installed Nix the easy way keeps working exactly as before.

## Verification

`dist plan` and a real `dist build --artifacts=local` confirm the `--package` invocation. `just actionlint` green (the two shellcheck notes in `release.yml` are pre-existing and in dist-generated output). The auth probe already in the action is what proves the netrc swap on a real runner: watch for `cachet: read auth probe returned 404` in this PR's jobs — 404 means authenticated, 401 means the credential didn't reach the daemon.
MD
)" 2>&1 | tail -2

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The docs/testing/lanes.toml table, the lane docs in docs/testing/, and the
# lane jobs in .github/workflows/ci.yml are a bijection (CLAUDE.md §8). This
# script fails the build on drift in any direction: a row without a doc, a
# doc without a row, a lane without a job, or a job that runs nothing. The

CI=".github/workflows/ci.yml"

content.text:
Pushed to main as `744dadc`. Once CI is green I'll tag `v0.0.8` and move `v0`, which is what actually puts the new installer in front of CI.

Meanwhile, back to your caching question — I have a partial answer and it's not what either of us assumed.

**The lanes are fine.** All 278 compilations in that clippy job happened inside `cachet-deps`; `cachet-clippy` compiled nothing. So crane's artifact reuse works — 465 paths substituted, 4 derivations built.

**The suspicion is `cachet-deps` itself.** It's built from `commonArgs`, whose `src` filter deliberately includes non-Rust files:

```nix
|| (rel == "clippy.toml")
|| (rel == ".config/nextest.toml")
|| (rel == "docs/openapi.yaml")
|| (lib.hasPrefix "fixtures/" rel)
|| (lib.hasSuffix ".snap" rel)
```

Those exist because the lanes genuinely need them. But if they reach the dummy source crane derives deps from, then editing a fixture, a snapshot, or `docs/openapi.yaml` invalidates all 278 crates — and `docs/openapi.yaml` changes on **every version bump**, including the one I just pushed.

That would explain "sad across the board" precisely: the deps cache gets busted by things that have nothing to do with dependencies.

I haven't proven it yet — my first attempt to diff the derivation hash used the wrong JSON shape. Want me to finish that measurement (touch a `.snap`, re-evaluate, compare hashes) once the release is out? It's a five-minute check and it either confirms a real fix or rules it out.

content.text:
I have the answer, and it's worse than "caching isn't working" — the caching is fine. Here's what I actually established:

- **The lanes are correct.** `cachet-clippy` compiles *nothing*; it decompresses `cargoArtifacts` and lints. Crane's reuse works.
- **`cachet-deps` is the whole cost**: 278 crates, 732 MiB of `target/`, rebuilt in the job.
- **It's cached properly.** That exact output (`23k2rc0…`) is in cachet right now: narinfo 200, signed `cachet.nox.so-1`, NAR 200 at 49 MB/s, and all three closure references present. The runner reads from that cache fine — 465 paths substituted in the same job.

So the artifact is available, signed, and trusted, and jobs rebuild it anyway.

The mundane explanation fits everything: **all 15 CI jobs start simultaneously.** None of them can substitute `cachet-deps` because nobody has pushed it yet — the push happens in each job's *Post* step, after the build. So every run that changes `Cargo.toml` or `Cargo.lock` pays the 278-crate dependency build **fifteen times in parallel**, and only afterwards does one of them win the race to publish it.

`Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` changed in #18, #19, #20, and the 0.0.8 bump — four times today. That's the sad feeling, and it's structural, not a cache misconfiguration.

The fix is a job dependency:

```yaml
deps:
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - uses: nox-systems/cachet/action@v0
    - run: nix develop --command nix build '.#checks.x86_64-linux.deps'

unit:
  needs: deps      # …and every other lane
```

One deps build per run instead of fifteen, pushed before the lanes start, so they all substitute it. Costs one job's latency up front; saves fourteen full dependency compiles whenever the lockfile moves.

I'd want to confirm the diagnosis before building it, and there's a clean experiment already queued: the 0.0.8 bump changed `Cargo.toml`, so the current main run will rebuild deps 15× (expected). The run *after* it won't change the lockfile — if that one substitutes instead of building, the diagnosis is confirmed and the fix is exactly the above. Want me to watch for that?

git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
Let a deploy with no terminal answer alchemy's prompt

Every CI deploy has been stopping at "Non-interactive terminal detected.
Pass --yes to approve", so staging has not deployed for days: alchemy
prints its plan and waits for an answer, and a GitHub runner has no way
to give one. The most recent run got as far as `Plan: 1 to update, 2 to
noop` and then refused to proceed.

The recipe now passes --yes when stdin is not a terminal. That is not a
decision taken away from anyone. Nobody is present to read that plan, so
the only outcomes available are approving it or failing, and failing is
what has been happening. A terminal still gets the prompt, because that
is where a human is there to read it.

`just destroy` is untouched and still asks either way. Deleting a
deployment is the operation whose confirmation is worth failing over.
MSG
git push -u origin fix/ci-deploys-can-approve -q 2>&1|tail -1; gh pr create --title "Let a deploy with no terminal answer alchemy's prompt" --body "$(cat <<'MD'
Staging has not deployed for days. Every CI deploy ends at:

```
Plan: 1 to update, 2 to noop
[Bucket] noop
[KV] noop
[Worker] update
[Worker/CACHET_GC_GRACE_MS] create

Non-interactive terminal detected. Pass --yes to approve, or set ALCHEMY_TUI=1 for the interactive UI.
```

Alchemy prints its plan and waits for approval. A GitHub runner has no terminal, so it cannot give one, and `just deploy` passes nothing that would. The deploy fails after doing all the work up to the plan.

`just deploy` now appends `--yes` when stdin is not a terminal.

That isn't removing a safety check from anyone. Nobody is present to read that plan, so the only two outcomes available to a non-interactive run are "approve" and "fail" — and "fail" is what has been happening. When there *is* a terminal, the prompt still appears, which is exactly where someone can read the plan and decide.

`just destroy` is deliberately untouched and still asks either way, terminal or not. Deleting a deployment is the operation whose confirmation is worth failing over, and `docs/DEPLOY.md` documents that it asks.

Verified `just scripts` (shellcheck over the recipe) and `just doc-manifest`.
MD
)" 2>&1 | tail -1

content.text:
[PR #21](https://github.com/nox-systems/cachet/pull/21) opened.

The failure is exact: alchemy prints its plan and waits, the runner has no terminal to answer with, so `just deploy` dies after doing all the work. `just deploy` now passes `--yes` only when stdin isn't a terminal — which isn't removing a safety check from anybody, since a non-interactive run's only two available outcomes are "approve" and "fail", and it's been failing. In a terminal the prompt still appears, where someone can actually read the plan.

`just destroy` is untouched and still asks either way; deleting a deployment is the one worth failing over, and DEPLOY.md documents that.

Three things in flight, so to be clear on state:

- **v0.0.8** tagged, release building. Once it publishes I'll move `v0`, which is what puts the new installer in front of CI.
- **PR #21** — the deploy fix above.
- **CI deps rebuild** — diagnosed, not yet fixed. All 15 jobs start together, none can substitute `cachet-deps` because nobody's pushed it yet, so every lockfile change costs 278 crate compiles ×15. The fix is a `deps` job the lanes `needs:`. I'd rather land it after confirming on a run that *doesn't* touch the lockfile.

One caveat worth stating plainly: I can't verify #21 before merging, for the same reason as the action change — the deploy workflow only runs on main after a green CI. Its first real test is the next push to main.
